chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Lays Al-Murady, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who grabs his beard while he is in Ihram, so he tampers with it, so some hairs get plucked off from it and they remain in his hand, out of error, or deliberately. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It does not harm him'.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.يَعْبَث: To tamper or play with (implying casual handling)

ai.seo_question: Does plucking beard hair invalidate Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that plucking beard hair while in Ihram incurs no penalty, distinguishing it from the more common prohibition of clipping hair. The Imam’s ruling emphasizes that the specific act of pulling out beard hairs (intif) is treated leniently, whether done by mistake or intentionally, reflecting the Shia juristic view that not all grooming acts carry the same weight of expiation (kaffarah). This highlights the nuanced differentiation between various types of hair removal in Shia fiqh compared to broader Sunni interpretations.
